Open • FLYBYME (Tim) opened about 2 minutes ago • 0 comments
Labels: bug


  Reported: "the first thing  mesh-core/src/catalog/index.ts  should do is    
  check                                                                       
  for auth if it needs it. nothing in that file tells me it needs auth. when i
  login it needs to be notified if it needs auth and then update."            
                                                                              
  All three halves of that are true.                                          
                                                                              
  Nothing declares it.  mesh-core/src/catalog/contract.ts:48  reads           
                                                                              
    export const NEEDS = needs('models', 'mesh', 'state', 'commands',         
  'windows', 'log');                                                          
    export const CONSUMES = consumes();                                       
                                                                              
  No  AUTH , no  consumes(AUTH) . The manifest — the thing that is supposed to
  make                                                                        
  a contribution's requirements visible — does not record that this           
  Application is                                                              
  unusable signed out.                                                        
                                                                              
  It fires anyway.  cx.models('part')  fetches during  start() . Signed out   
  every one of those is a guaranteed 401, so the first thing a person sees is 
   Failed to load catalog parts (http): ...  rather than a sign-in prompt.    
                                                                              
  And nothing retries.  AuthApi.session  is a  Signal<Session | null> , so the
  information is available and reactive — but no consumer is subscribed, so   
  signing                                                                     
  in leaves every collection sitting on the error it got before there was a   
  session. The page looks broken until it is reloaded by hand.                
                                                                              
  The gate-driven half of the fix (a collection knowing whether a call needs a
  session, rather than being told by hand) depends on #39. The declaration and
  the                                                                         
  reload-on-sign-in do not.

    Tiled mode tiles; the kernel stops laying out parts' forms
    
    Two bugs from using the console, one root cause each.
    
    **Tiled mode did nothing.** Tiling ran off the Application's declared split
    tree, and nothing in mesh-core declares a tile — so `rectOf` had no tile to
    answer with and never assigned a position. Every window kept the box it
    already had: "i go to tiled mode and the windows are stacked like when you
    first open the app." This was fixed once already, in the wrong direction: the
    original bug blanked the page, that was repaired by falling back to what
    windowed mode shows, and a test was then written asserting `rectOf` stayed
    undefined — encoding "tiled mode does nothing" as intent. Fourth time a test
    has done that here.
    
    `gridLayout()` generates a layout when none is declared, tiles named by window
    id, built from open order rather than stack order so focusing a window does not
    rearrange every pane. A declared layout still wins outright.
    
    **A form stacked its fields into a column.** `kernel.css` carried
    `form { flex-direction: column }` — the one rule in the file that set layout
    rather than appearance. chrome's sign-in form declared `display: flex` inline
    and not a direction, and an inline style only wins the properties it names, so
    the kernel kept the direction. Signing in swapped the form for a div, which the
    rule does not match, and the row appeared.
    
    An appearance default is a look a part overrides in one property. A layout
    default is a second author for a box the part believes it owns.
    
    Also: the viewport measures the window host rather than the mount root, with a
    ResizeObserver on it, since the chrome bar's own height changing fires no
    window resize.

    The staleness check compared the wrong two hashes

    response.
    
    client.ts compared api.exposure against x-exposure -- both gate hashes. But a
    generated client cannot know a site's gates: a part declares what it *calls*,
    never the gate it runs at, so mesh-serve client writes auth: 'public'
    uniformly and the part's exposure is computed over that placeholder. The two
    cannot match by construction, so every gated site reported stale forever.

    shapeHash, emitted it from the generator, and sent x-exposure-shape on every
    response -- and nothing in the kernel ever read it. Another field emitted for
    a reader that was never connected.

    generated before D4 carries no shapeHash and an older API sends no header, and
    either absence skips the check rather than failing it. Unverifiable is weaker
    than verified and far better than refusing every call -- and it resolves itself
    on the next regenerate.

Author: FLYBYME <mangoraft@gmail.com>

    Collections follow the session (FLYBYME/surfdns#40)
    
    A collection (`models`) must react to the session:
    1. Reload on session arrival: When the session transitions from absent to
       present, a collection that previously failed for want of one (HTTP 401
       unauthorized) reloads automatically.
    2. Clear rows on sign-out: When the session transitions from present to
       absent, the collection immediately clears data and rows (`data: undefined`,
       `rows: []`, `status: 'idle'`). This eliminates data leaks between sessions
       and avoids displaying another user's rows after sign-out.
    3. User switching: When user switches (User A -> User B), rows for User A are
       immediately cleared and rows for User B are fetched.
    4. Suppress failing calls & Seam for #39: When a collection fails for auth
       and the session is absent, `shouldFetch()` returns false on query signal
       changes, avoiding spamming calls certain to fail while leaving a clean seam
       for `ExposureDescriptor.gate` (FLYBYME/surfdns#39). Explicit `refetch()`
       bypasses this suppression.
    5. In-flight 401 race handling: If an unauthenticated request returns 401 while
       a session arrived in the meantime, it triggers an immediate reload with the
       new session.
    6. Manifest session declaration: Applications can declare `session?: 'required' | 'optional'`,
       distinct from `consumes(AUTH)`. Manifest records this in `manifest.sessions`.
    7. Zero auth dependencies for unauthenticated sites: A site without `AuthExtension`
       boots cleanly and loads public collections without auth dependencies.
    
    Bump kernel patch version 0.15.2 -> 0.15.3 in package.json and mesh.json.
